title: The graded quiz, replayed
intro: The certificate quiz, rebuilt from my answer key — including the one I missed.

questions.prompt: What role does quantization play in inference efficiency?
choices: It retrains the model on smaller data
It stores weights in lower-precision formats, cutting memory and data movement
It caches previous answers to skip generation
It splits the model across more GPUs
questions.explanation: Fewer bits per weight → less memory AND fewer bytes streamed HBM→SRAM every step.

questions.prompt: Why is the KV cache critical in modern LLM inference?
choices: It stores the model weights closer to the tensor cores
It keeps previously computed keys & values so past tokens aren't recomputed
It caches full responses for repeated questions
It reduces the number of layers per forward pass
questions.explanation: A new token needs the K/V of every past token — cached once, reused every step, at every layer.

questions.prompt: How does continuous batching improve GPU utilization?
choices: It pads all requests to the same length
It dynamically fills freed slots at the token level, so no slot idles behind a long request
It runs each request on its own GPU
It processes requests strictly in arrival order
questions.explanation: Token-level scheduling: the moment a request finishes, a queued one takes its slot on the next step.

choices: Slow attention math for long contexts
KV-cache waste from fragmentation and max-length over-reservation
Weights not fitting on a single GPU
Networking overhead between replicas
questions.explanation: Fixed-size blocks tracked by a block table replace contiguous max-length slabs — recovering the 60–80% of cache that naive allocation wasted.

questions.prompt: ⚠️ The one I missed — key difference between W8A16 and W8A8?
choices: Weight-only quantization degrades accuracy less than weight+activation
W8A16 speeds up data movement; W8A8 speeds up data movement AND tensor-core compute
W8A8 only works during training
W8A16 requires no calibration data
questions.explanation: The trap is answer A: with calibrated methods BOTH preserve accuracy — the schemes differ in **which bottleneck they speed up**, not quality. Weight-only halves the bytes moved; adding activations unlocks low-precision tensor cores for the math itself.

questions.prompt: How do SLOs influence benchmarking and deployment?
choices: They are fixed industry standards every deployment must meet
They are measurable per-use-case targets (TTFT/ITL/latency at percentiles) that benchmarks are judged against
They only apply to training pipelines
They replace the need for benchmarking
questions.explanation: Define them BEFORE benchmarking: a chatbot might need TTFT ≤200 ms @ p99 while RAG relaxes to 300 ms — same metrics, different thresholds.

questions.prompt: What is the calibration dataset for in GPTQ / AWQ?
choices: Fine-tuning the model on domain data
Representative text that reveals which weights matter, so quantization can protect them
Measuring throughput under load
Generating the model card
questions.explanation: A few hundred samples run through the model let GPTQ measure sensitivity (Hessian) and AWQ spot high-activation weights — protecting what matters and compressing the rest.
